summary: Crow's nest on Dead Horse Rim, Fremont-Winema NF, Lake County OR: patrol use in 1911, crow's nest dated 1913, listed abandoned; trail #139 crosses the rim.

facts.status_note: Listed as abandoned. Firelookout.com says the crow's nest was still there in 1993; no later source checked.

access.note: Forest Service trail #139 travels over the rim. No source says whether any of the lookout remains at the summit.

visit.trail_note: Dead Horse Rim Trail #139 goes up and over the rim to Forest Road 34 and connects to Lakes Loop Trail #140 at the summit.

events.note: Lester E. Elder, Forest Guard, used the point as a patrol lookout in July and August. A trail to the rim from Deadhorse Lake was blazed that August.
Firelookout.com dates a crow's nest at this site to 1913.
A June 3, 1915 note said fire-finding instruments would be placed on Dead Horse Rim and Drakes Peak.

evidence.supports: 1911 patrol lookout used by Forest Guard Lester E. Elder in July and August
evidence.quote: 1911: This point was used as a patrol lookout by Lester E. Elder, Forest Guard, during the months of July and August.

evidence.supports: Trail blazed to the rim from Deadhorse Lake in August 1911
evidence.quote: A trail was blazed to the top of the rim from Deadhorse Lake in August.

evidence.supports: 1915 note: fire finding instruments to be placed on Dead Horse Rim and Drakes Peak
evidence.quote: Later on the fire finding instruments will be placed on Dead Horse Rim and Drakes Peak.

evidence.supports: Site in Fremont National Forest, Lake County
1913 crow's nest; still there in 1993; abandoned
Location 18 miles northeast of Bly, Lake County, Oregon
FFLOS Oregon list: Dead Horse Lake row, crow's nest, abandoned
Trail #139 goes up and over Dead Horse Rim to Forest Road 34
evidence.quote: This trail route travels up and over Dead Horse Rim to Forest Road 34.

evidence.supports: Trail #139 is the only improved access into the Dead Horse and Augur Creek Roadless Areas
evidence.quote: It provides the only improved access into the Dead Horse and Augur Creek Roadless Areas and the Dead Horse Rim Whitebark Pine Research Area.

evidence.supports: Forest Service page names the unit Fremont-Winema National Forest
Date of the fire-finding instruments note: June 3, 1915

corrections.why: The Forest Service trail page names the unit Fremont-Winema National Forest. The brief and the older Forest Lookouts page use Fremont National Forest.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts page records a 1911 patrol use of the point. Firelookout.com dates a crow's nest to 1913. The sources do not say whether the 1911 patrol point and the 1913 crow's nest were the same structure. The story reports both dates.

sources.title: Dead Horse Rim Trail #139
sources.publisher: Fremont-Winema National Forest, U.S. Forest Service

notes_for_editor: Named Dead Horse on firelookout.com, Deadhorse Rim on Forest Lookouts, and Dead Horse Lake on the FFLOS Oregon list. The brief's coordinates (42.52987, -120.78553) sit about 2.3 km south of the FFLOS point (42.55007, -120.78301); check on a map. The 1915 entry says instruments would be placed, not that they were. The last sighting of the crow's nest is 1993 per firelookout.com. No photo added.
